model: IPS 4000 pumping system controller - variable secondary
applies_to: Armstrong IPS 4000 controllers set up for variable secondary pumping: up to 8 pumps and 16 control zones.
summary: The IPS 4000 runs a group of variable-speed pumps. The variable secondary version has no chiller/boiler points; its BACnet list covers start/stop, pump Hand/Off/Auto commands, hand speeds, zone setpoints and values, pump speed, power, energy, RPM, head and flow, run hours, and no-flow and drive alarms.
notes: 121 rows printed as Reserved are left out.
The cover prints File No 90.761; the file name on Armstrong's site is 90-9761.
Analog descriptions give the scaled range from the Represent column; the PDF also prints a raw integer range.

This list is for communication interface ver 2.1.0. Older IPS 4000 controllers (interface ver 1.0.0, Data Points 90.976, and the legacy 90.972) have their own data-point sheets; check which one matches the controller.
The PDF table is on pages 14-23.

integration.summary: Start and stop the IPS 4000 with BV 1 Remote Start, write the zone setpoints (AV 1-16) and read BI 110 IPS On Status, the active zone value, system flow and head, and BI 1 General Alarm. Reset alarms with BV 32. The BMS can also put each pump in Hand, Off or Auto (BV 2-25), set hand speeds and write zone values (bas Zone pv AVs).

minimum_points.name: Active Zone PV
minimum_points.why: Value of the zone in control

integration.enable: BV 1 Remote Start (0 = Stop, 1 = Start). The Set Pump Hand/Off/Auto BVs are momentary commands that change one pump's mode.
integration.remote_sensors: The bas Zone 1-16 pv AVs (48-63) are writable, so the BMS can supply zone values. The data-points sheet does not say how the controller chooses between BMS and wired values.
setup: The sheet lists BACnet TCP/IP and BACnet MS/TP. For BACnet IP use UDP port 47808 (0xBAC0).
The device instance and MS/TP settings are not given in the sheet.
gotchas: Set Pump Hand/Off/Auto BVs are momentary: write 1 to change the mode, and read the pump mode BIs to confirm it.
Design flow/head, BEP and dead-band AVs are commissioning settings; don't write them cyclically.
Units for pressure, temperature and flow follow the controller's unit setting.
